summary: Part 1 (00:00-03:41) of the seller training "7.0 Refund policy (Seller)". Pierre walks through the Returns Refund Policy overview slide (Contract clause 9.1): four stages with working-day (WD) deadlines (Solve 5 WD; Warning 6 WD AE/ZA/others and 7 WD SA; Closing 8 WD AE/ZA/others and 9 WD SA; Collecting, SA only), the working-day clock rules (weekends excluded, resolution request stops the clock, worked Monday/Wednesday/Friday example), then the "Which stages count against you" timeline slide, which lists the stages that run the seller clock in SA (9 stages) and in AE/ZA/others (3 stages), and the SA pickup steps. Part 1 ends mid-sentence at 03:40 ("create a new ROE bill and to"), so the SA collection-failed explanation is incomplete here.

terms.meaning: Working day. Defined in the 'How the clock works' box as the sum of the hours during working days the claim spends on the seller side only.
The timer that counts the working days. It runs only while the claim sits on the seller side; it is stopped while Revibe holds the claim.
Stage 1, all markets: the seller has 5 WD to solve the return.
Stage 2: the return is still not solved, so the seller gets a warning and the return turns yellow marked in the app (6 WD in AE/ZA/others, 7 WD in SA).
Stage 3: the return is still not solved, so a full refund is issued to the customer and the claim closes against the seller (8 WD in AE/ZA/others, 9 WD in SA).
Stage 4, Saudi Arabia only: Revibe collects the device; once received Revibe refunds the customer and credits the seller. The card shows '9 WD +' (the + is not explained in part 1).
What the seller creates when there is any issue with the device. The clock stops straight away and restarts only when the resolution is solved.
How a return at the warning stage shows in the app.
The bill the seller creates in SA. The card says 'The AWB is yours to create - nothing moves until you issue it.' The expansion is not shown or spoken in part 1.
The period in which the customer must hand the device to the delivery company. Not counted against the seller in any market.
In SA, the stage where the seller creates the bill and schedules the pick-up time. Counted against the seller (dark blue dot on the SA row).
In SA, the stage where the customer does not succeed in handing the device to the delivery company. Counted against the seller (dark blue bar on the SA row).
Market codes on screen. The trainer says UAE and South Africa for the first two, and the flags on screen match. SA is Saudi Arabia (the trainer says 'Saudi Arabia' for SA).
The company, and the app in which returns are raised and claims are tracked.
The contract clause the returns refund policy slide is labelled with.
